reason: The hypothesis proposes specific mechanisms (interfacial oxide formation, reduced interdiffusion, improved adhesion) and broad applicability across environments, but cites no prior evidence to support these claims for Cr coatings on Zr-alloys. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover these specific interfacial behaviors in this system.
premises: Reactive element addition forms a stable oxide layer at the coating-substrate interface
This interfacial oxide layer reduces Cr-Zr interdiffusion
This interfacial oxide layer improves coating adhesion
The mechanism is effective under both subcritical water and high-temperature steam (300-1200°C)
